lines: I heard arrows, axes, and shouting. Then I saw you still standing for us.
Good aim is choosing what matters under pressure. You chose the village.
You picked the right target when the raid pressed in.
I saw you move where the arrows were falling. That takes nerve.
Every raider stopped early is a home spared later.
You helped turn the fight before it reached the square.
We need eyes on every road before the bell rings.
A clear retreat matters as much as a strong wall.
Keep spare arrows in more than one building.
The rooftop has a view, but no cover from crossbows.
Mark the weak fences while there is time to repair them.
Children and animals need shelter before the fighting starts.
The fields could give us warning if someone watches them.
Nobody should defend a gate alone.
The target lane gives archers room without blocking the road.
Dry strings belong near every guard post.
We should practice moving the wounded before the next alarm.
A stack of blocks near the gate could save lives.
After every attack, write down what failed.
You gave the village more than a good shot. You gave us time.
